claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The assembly of heterochromatin complexes is directed by an increase in odr-1 22G siRNA.
claims.source: The assembly of heterochromatin complexes is directed by an increase in the odr-1 small interfering RNA (siRNA), consisting of 22 nucleotides starting with a 5′ guanosine (22G), whose synthesis requires the 3′−5′ exonuclease activity of MUT-7 in butanone-trained animals (Juang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Loss of functional mut-7 ortholog in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to defective post-transcriptional gene silencing.
claims.source: In Arabidopsis thaliana, loss of the functional mut-7 ortholog encoding a WS-like exonuclease (WEX) leads to defective post-transcriptional gene silencing (Glazov et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Glazov et al., 2003.

claims.claim: MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 are required for animals to learn to ignore butanone after odor training.
claims.source: Strains that lacked MUT-7 or CeWRN-1 were analyzed in the chemotaxis assay, and we found that their odor-trained CI was not only greater than half of the naïve CI but also significantly differed from the CIs of odor-trained wild-type animals (Figure 1B, lower figure), suggesting that MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 are required for animals to learn.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from chemotaxis assays shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 act in the same pathway in AWC neurons to promote olfactory learning.
claims.source: To examine whether MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 act in the same genetic pathway, we generated mut-7;Cewrn-1 double mutants and found that the ability of the double-mutant animals to alter their response to butanone was similar to that of single-mutant animals (Figure 1B, lower). Thus, the data indicate that MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 act in the same pathway in AWC neurons to promote olfactory learning.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by genetic epistasis data from double mutant analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The mut-7(ne4255) allele with E437K mutation reduces the activity of the 3′−5′ exonuclease.
claims.source: An allele of mut-7(ne4255) with a missense mutation at E437K has been predicted to reduce the activity of the 3′−5′ exonuclease by interrupting the predicted Mg2+ binding domain (Gu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gu et al., 2009, which predicts the effect of this mutation.

claims.claim: mut-7(ne4255) mutant animals are defective in butanone chemotaxis.
claims.source: mut-7(ne4255) mutant animals were shown to be defective in butanone chemotaxis (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Worms carrying the W812 Amber mutation in MUT-7 showed reduced 22G RNA levels.
claims.source: Worms carrying the W812 Amber mutation in MUT-7 showed reduced 22G RNA levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: mut-7(pk204) mutants are able to show chemotaxis toward butanone but unable to learn to ignore this odor after it was paired with starvation.
claims.source: Worms carrying the W812 Amber mutation in MUT-7 showed reduced 22G RNA levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and although they were able to show chemotaxis toward butanone, they were unable to learn to ignore this odor after it was paired with starvation (Figure 1C; Juang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and cited from Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The expression of GFP-MUT-7 in AWC cells restored odor learning in mut-7(pk204) mutant animals.
claims.source: We previously found that the expression of MUT-7 with GFP appended to its N-terminus (GFP-MUT-7 in Figure 2A, upper) specifically in AWC cells restored odor learning in mut-7(pk204) mutant animals (Figure 2B, fourth pair).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The expression of GFP-MUT-7 in AWC restored odr-1 22G RNA levels in mut-7(pk204) odor-trained worms.
claims.source: The expression of GFP-MUT-7 in AWC also restored odr-1 22G RNA levels in mut-7(pk204) odor-trained worms (Figure 2C, third dataset) (Juang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and cited from Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Prolonged odor exposure decreased odr-1 mRNA levels in wild-type animals.
claims.source: Indeed, we used quantitative real-time PCR to probe odr-1 mRNA and found that prolonged odor exposure decreased odr-1 mRNA levels in wild-type animals, while odr-1 mRNA levels were insensitive to odor exposure in mut-7(pk204) mutant animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: odr-1 mRNA levels were insensitive to odor exposure in mut-7(pk204) mutant animals.
claims.source: Indeed, we used quantitative real-time PCR to probe odr-1 mRNA and found that prolonged odor exposure decreased odr-1 mRNA levels in wild-type animals, while odr-1 mRNA levels were insensitive to odor exposure in mut-7(pk204) mutant animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: GFP-tagged ODR-1 was concentrated in the flattened ciliated end of the AWC neuron.
claims.source: Furthermore, we used a CRISPR-Cas9 system to generate an integrated line expressing ODR-1::GFP under the control of the endogenous odr-1 promoter. GFP-tagged ODR-1 was concentrated in the flattened ciliated end of the AWC neuron (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The fluorescence intensity of ODR-1::GFP in naïve wild-type animals was significantly brighter than in odor-trained wild-type animals.
claims.source: The fluorescence intensity in naïve wild-type animals was significantly brighter than the fluorescence of GFP in odor-trained wild-type animals (Figure 2D, top).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: No significant difference in ODR-1::GFP expression induced by odor exposure was observed in mut-7(pk204) mutants.
claims.source: In contrast, no significant difference in GFP expression induced by odor exposure was observed in the mut-7(pk204) mutants (Figure 2D, bottom).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: MUT-7 is required in the synthesis of odr-1 22G RNA after prolonged odor treatment to downregulate the expression of both odr-1 mRNA and ODR-1 protein.
claims.source: These results confirm that MUT-7 is required in the synthesis of odr-1 22G RNA after prolonged odor treatment to specifically downregulate the expression of both the odr-1 mRNA and the ODR-1 protein.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the combined results from RT-qPCR and fluorescence microscopy experiments.

claims.claim: Animals in which MUT-7 was restricted to the cytoplasm showed an increase in odr-1.7 22G RNA levels to the same level found in wild type when odor trained.
claims.source: We found that animals in which MUT-7 was restricted to the cytoplasm (CterGFP-MUT-7) showed an increase in the odr-1.7 22G RNA levels to the same level found in the wild type when they were odor trained (Figure 2C, first versus fourth datasets).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Animals with cytoplasm-restricted MUT-7 exhibited wild-type levels of odr-1.7 22G RNA but were not able to learn as well as wild types.
claims.source: This was interesting because although they exhibited wild-type levels of odr-1.7 22G RNA, these animals were not able to learn as well as the wild types (Figure 2B, first versus fifth pairs of bars).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by combined data from RT-qPCR (Figure 2C) and behavioral assays (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: Restricting MUT-7 to the nucleus blocked the odor-dependent increases in both 22G RNA and learning.
claims.source: By contrast, restricting MUT-7 to the nucleus (NLS-GFP-MUT-7) blocked the odor-dependent increases in both 22G RNA (Figure 2C, first versus fifth dataset) and learning (Figure 2B, first versus sixth pairs of bars).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by combined data from RT-qPCR (Figure 2C) and behavioral assays (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: Expressing both CterGFP-MUT-7 and NLS-GFP-MUT-7 in mut-7(pk204) mutants restored both 22G RNA levels and odor learning.
claims.source: Importantly, each version of MUT-7 was functional, as expressing both CterGFP-MUT-7 and NLS-GFP-MUT-7 in the mut-7(pk204) mutants restored both 22G RNA levels and odor learning (Figure 2B, seventh pair of bars, and Figure 2C, sixth dataset).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by combined data from RT-qPCR (Figure 2C) and behavioral assays (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: 22G RNA production is not sufficient to cause odor learning.
claims.source: Thus, 22G RNA production is not sufficient to cause odor learning, and MUT-7 must perform an additional role in the nucleus, because when it is restricted from the nucleus, animals do not learn.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that cytoplasmic MUT-7 produces 22G RNA but does not fully restore learning.

claims.claim: MUT-7 must perform an additional role in the nucleus for odor learning to occur.
claims.source: Thus, 22G RNA production is not sufficient to cause odor learning, and MUT-7 must perform an additional role in the nucleus, because when it is restricted from the nucleus, animals do not learn.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that nuclear MUT-7 is required for learning even when 22G RNA is produced.

claims.claim: Cytoplasmic MUT-7 functions in the small RNA synthesis process.
claims.source: Taken together, our behavioral and RT-qPCR results indicate that cytoplasmic MUT-7 may function in the small RNA synthesis process.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined behavioral and RT-qPCR results.

claims.claim: MUT-7 acts in a different way in the nucleus compared to the cytoplasm.
claims.source: These results also provide insight that MUT-7 acts in a different way in the nucleus.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that nuclear and cytoplasmic MUT-7 have distinct functions.

claims.claim: The two pools of MUT-7 must act in coordination to promote olfactory learning.
claims.source: Moreover, the two pools of MUT-7 must (indirectly) act in coordination to promote olfactory learning.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that both nuclear and cytoplasmic MUT-7 are required for full learning.

claims.claim: Asymmetric expression of STR-2 was observed in more than 96% of animals expressing CterGFP-MUT-7 or NLS-GFP-MUT-7.
claims.source: To determine whether the various versions of MUT-7 affect this cell fate, STR-2-driven DsRed fluorescence was expressed in CterGFP-MUT-7 or NLS-GFP-MUT-7 transgenic animals, and asymmetric expression of STR-2 was observed in more than 96% of tested animals (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: The impairment of behavioral plasticity in adult animals carrying CterGFP-MUT-7 or NLS-GFP-MUT-7 is not due to changes in cell fate.
claims.source: This result suggests that the impairment of behavioral plasticity in adult animals carrying CterGFP-MUT-7 or NLS-GFP-MUT-7 is not due to changes in cell fate.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that cell fate is normal in these animals.

claims.claim: Mutations in the PKG consensus sites of MUT-7 caused defects in odor learning.
claims.source: Mutations in the PKG consensus sites of MUT-7 caused defects in odor learning (Figure 3A; Juang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3A and cited from Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: MUT-7 acts downstream of nuclear EGL-4.
claims.source: Our previous genetic epistasis experiments indicated that MUT-7 acts downstream of nuclear EGL-4 (Juang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Juang et al., 2013, which describes genetic epistasis experiments.

claims.claim: Only 1% of buffer-trained animals showed a reconstituted BiFC fluorescent signal between MUT-7 and EGL-4 in the AWC nucleus.
claims.source: We observed that only 1% of buffer-trained animals showed a reconstituted fluorescent signal in the AWC nucleus and that this percentage rose to 75% after prolonged odor training (Figure 3B and C, first row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claims.claim: 75% of odor-trained animals showed a reconstituted BiFC fluorescent signal between MUT-7 and EGL-4 in the AWC nucleus.
claims.source: We observed that only 1% of buffer-trained animals showed a reconstituted fluorescent signal in the AWC nucleus and that this percentage rose to 75% after prolonged odor training (Figure 3B and C, first row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claims.claim: The BiFC signal between MUT-7 and EGL-4 in each butanone-trained animal was seen in only one AWC neuron.
claims.source: Importantly, the BiFC signal in each butanone-trained animal was seen in only one AWC neuron.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC microscopy observations.

claims.claim: Butanone is sensed by only one AWC neuron.
claims.source: This reflects the fact that butanone is sensed by only one AWC (Wes and Bargmann, 2001).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wes and Bargmann, 2001.

claims.claim: 86% of odor-trained animals expressing NLS::EGL-4 and MUT-7 exhibited the BiFC signal.
claims.source: In addition, we tested constitutively nuclear EGL-4 tagged with the Venus C-terminus (NLS::EGL-4) in naïve animals expressing MUT-7 tagged with the Venus N-terminus, and 86% of odor-trained animals exhibited the BiFC signal (Figure 3C, third row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: EGL-4 associates either directly or in a protein complex with MUT-7 in the AWC nucleus of odor-trained worms.
claims.source: These results indicate that EGL-4 associates either directly or in a protein complex with MUT-7 in the AWC nucleus of odor-trained worms.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results showing interaction between EGL-4 and MUT-7.

claims.claim: Nonphosphorylatable forms of MUT-7 with all seven PKG phosphorylation sites mutated to alanine failed to reconstitute the BiFC signal with EGL-4.
claims.source: Thus, we performed a similar BiFC analysis with MUT-7 variants in which all seven of the predicted PKG phosphorylation sites were mutated to nonphosphorylatable alanine residues (Figure 3A). These nonphosphorylatable forms of MUT-7 failed to reconstitute the BiFC signal (Figure 3C, second and fourth rows).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The single S883A mutation in MUT-7 was sufficient to block BiFC fluorescence with EGL-4.
claims.source: The single S883A mutation (at a site deleted in the pk204 allele of mut-7) was sufficient to block BiFC fluorescence (Figure 3C, sixth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The phosphorylated form of MUT-7 is bound by EGL-4 in the AWC nucleus.
claims.source: Taken together, these data lead us to propose that the phosphorylated form of MUT-7 is bound by EGL-4 in the AWC nucleus and that EGL-4 kinase may be responsible for phosphorylating MUT-7.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results showing that phosphorylation sites are required for the interaction.

claims.claim: EGL-4 kinase may be responsible for phosphorylating MUT-7.
claims.source: Taken together, these data lead us to propose that the phosphorylated form of MUT-7 is bound by EGL-4 in the AWC nucleus and that EGL-4 kinase may be responsible for phosphorylating MUT-7.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the inference from BiFC results.

claims.claim: A point mutation in MUT-7 (S516A) does not affect learning.
claims.source: As a control, a point mutation in MUT-7 (S516A) that does not affect learning (Figure 3A, fifth pair for behavior) (Juang et al., 2013) was shown to not disrupt BiFC between EGL-4 and MUT-7 (Figure 3C, fifth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3A and cited from Juang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The S516A mutation in MUT-7 does not disrupt BiFC between EGL-4 and MUT-7.
claims.source: As a control, a point mutation in MUT-7 (S516A) that does not affect learning (Figure 3A, fifth pair for behavior) (Juang et al., 2013) was shown to not disrupt BiFC between EGL-4 and MUT-7 (Figure 3C, fifth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Only 11% of odor-trained transgenic animals expressing MUT-7(W812Amber) showed the BiFC signal with EGL-4.
claims.source: We found that only 11% of odor-trained transgenic animals showed the BiFC signal (Figure 3C, seventh row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The production of odr-1 22G RNA by processes involving MUT-7 in the cytoplasm is required for the association between EGL-4 and MUT-7 in the AWC nucleus.
claims.source: This result suggests that the production of odr-1 22G RNA by processes that involve MUT-7 in the cytoplasm is required for the association between EGL-4 and MUT-7 in the AWC nucleus.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results with the W812Amber mutant.

claims.claim: The cytoplasmic and nuclear pools of MUT-7 do not have to move between compartments to promote odor learning.
claims.source: We have presented evidence that the cytoplasmic and nuclear pools of MUT-7 do not have to move between the compartments to promote odor learning (Figure 2B; the co-expression of NLS-GFP-MUT-7 and CterGFP-MUT-7 in mut-7(pk204) animals rescues mut-7 learning defects).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: NRDE-3 shuttles 22G siRNA from the cytoplasm to the nucleus in the nuclear RNA silencing pathway.
claims.source: One candidate potentially mediating this process is the Argonaut NRDE-3, which shuttles 22G siRNA from the cytoplasm to the nucleus in the nuclear RNA silencing pathway (Guang et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Guang et al., 2008.

claims.claim: odr-1 22G RNAs are loaded onto NRDE-3 in butanone odor-trained worms.
claims.source: A previous coimmunoprecipitation analysis revealed that odr-1 22G RNAs are loaded onto NRDE-3 in butanone odor-trained worms (Juang et al., 2013)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Juang et al., 2013, which describes coimmunoprecipitation results.

claims.claim: The BiFC signal between MUT-7 and EGL-4 was not detected in nrde-3(gg66) mutant animals in either naïve or odor-trained conditions.
claims.source: We expressed MUT-7 tagged with the Venus N-terminus and EGL-4 tagged with the Venus C-terminus in nrde-3(gg66) mutant animals lacking NRDE-3. We found that the BiFC signal was not detected in either naïve or odor-trained transgenic worms (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, first row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: 86% of odor-trained wild-type worms co-expressing NLS::EGL-4 and constitutively nuclear MUT-7 showed a BiFC signal.
claims.source: Furthermore, we observed that 86% of odor-trained wild-type worms co-expressing NLS::EGL-4 and constitutively nuclear MUT-7 tagged with the Venus N-terminus (NLS::MUT-7) showed a BiFC signal (Figure 3C, last row)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Only 5% of odor-trained nrde-3(gg66) mutant worms expressing NLS::EGL-4 and NLS::MUT-7 showed a BiFC signal.
claims.source: but that only 5% of odor-trained nrde-3(gg66) mutant worms expressing the same constructs showed a BiFC signal (Figure 4D, first row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: The import of 22G RNAs into the nucleus via NRDE-3 is required for the association between nuclear MUT-7 and EGL-4.
claims.source: Taken together, these observations indicate that the import of 22G RNAs into the nucleus via NRDE-3 is required for the association between nuclear MUT-7 and EGL-4.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results in nrde-3 mutants.

claims.claim: Strains lacking CeWRN-1 were unable to learn to ignore butanone after training.
claims.source: Olfactory behavioral analysis revealed that strains lacking CeWRN-1 were unable to learn to ignore butanone after training (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: GFP expression under the control of the Cewrn-1 promoter showed a signal in many cells, including the pair of AWC neurons.
claims.source: The expression pattern of CeWRN-1 has not been characterized in vivo, so we placed GFP expression under the control of the Cewrn-1 promoter and observed a GFP signal in many cells, including the pair of AWC neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The expression of CeWRN-1 protein in AWCs rescued the learning defects of the Cewrn-1(gk99) mutant.
claims.source: To determine whether CeWRN-1 acts in AWC neurons to regulate odor sensing and learning, the CeWRN-1 protein was expressed in AWCs and rescued the learning defects of the Cewrn-1(gk99) mutant (Figure 4B, bottom).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral rescue data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: GFP-tagged CeWRN-1 stained the AWC nucleus.
claims.source: Furthermore, GFP-tagged CeWRN-1 stained the AWC nucleus (Figure 4B, top).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: CeWRN-1 acts within AWC neurons to promote olfactory plasticity.
claims.source: These data indicate that CeWRN-1 acts within AWC neurons to promote olfactory plasticity.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue experiments and localization data.

claims.claim: The wild-type pattern of asymmetric STR-2 expression was observed in all tested Cewrn-1 mutant animals.
claims.source: This is unlikely to be due to a change in AWC cell fate because the wild-type pattern of asymmetric STR-2 expression was observed in all tested animals (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: GFP-tagged EGL-4 entered the nucleus of AWC neurons in Cewrn-1(gk99) animals that had been trained with butanone.
claims.source: We found that GFP-tagged EGL-4 entered the nucleus of AWC neurons in Cewrn-1(gk99) animals that had been trained with butanone (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: CeWRN-1 does not regulate EGL-4 nuclear entry.
claims.source: Thus, CeWRN-1 does not regulate EGL-4 nuclear entry.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that EGL-4 enters the nucleus in Cewrn-1 mutants.

claims.claim: Less than 2% of transgenic animals expressing CeWRN-1 and EGL-4 BiFC constructs showed a fluorescent signal under either naïve or trained conditions.
claims.source: To test this hypothesis, we appended the N-terminal half of Venus to CeWRN-1 and expressed this construct in a strain-expressing EGL-4 tagged with the C-terminal half of Venus. Less than 2% of transgenic animals under either naïve or trained conditions showed a fluorescent signal (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, second row)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: CeWRN-1 and EGL-4 do not interact directly.
claims.source: Less than 2% of transgenic animals under either naïve or trained conditions showed a fluorescent signal (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, second row), suggesting that the CeWRN-1 and EGL-4 do not interact directly.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of BiFC signal.

claims.claim: 46% of odor-trained worms co-expressing CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 BiFC constructs showed the BiFC signal.
claims.source: To explore whether nematode MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 could interact, the BiFC constructs for CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 were co-expressed in wild-type animals, and 46% of odor-trained worms showed the BiFC signal, in contrast to <4% of buffer-trained control worms (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, third row; Figure 4C, top).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Less than 4% of buffer-trained control worms co-expressing CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 BiFC constructs showed the BiFC signal.
claims.source: To explore whether nematode MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 could interact, the BiFC constructs for CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 were co-expressed in wild-type animals, and 46% of odor-trained worms showed the BiFC signal, in contrast to <4% of buffer-trained control worms (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, third row; Figure 4C, top).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Only 3% of naïve and odor-trained nrde-3(gg99) mutants expressing CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 BiFC constructs exhibited the BiFC signal.
claims.source: In addition, the same BiFC constructs were expressed in nrde-3(gg99) mutants, and only 3% of naïve and odor-rained worms exhibited the BiFC signal (Figure 4D, second row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: CeWRN-1 may associate with nuclear MUT-7 in the presence of NRDE-3.
claims.source: These results indicate that CeWRN-1 may associate with nuclear MUT-7 in the presence of NRDE-3 and that they may mediate olfactory learning together.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results in wild-type and nrde-3 mutant backgrounds.

claims.claim: Very few naïve or odor-trained animals expressing MUT-7 and HPL-2 BiFC constructs showed BiFC.
claims.source: To distinguish between these possibilities, we first asked whether MUT-7 and HPL-2 are in close enough association in the nucleus to reconstitute fluorescence (BiFC). We found that very few naïve or odor-trained animals showed BiFC (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, fourth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: MUT-7 and HPL-2 are unlikely to be associated even after odor training.
claims.source: Thus, MUT-7 and HPL-2 are unlikely to be associated even after odor training.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of BiFC signal between MUT-7 and HPL-2.

claims.claim: 67% of odor-trained hpl-2 null animals showed BiFC between EGL-4 and MUT-7.
claims.source: Second, we asked if the EGL-4-MUT-7 association requires HPL-2. We found that, in hpl-2 null animals, 67% of odor-trained animals showed BiFC, in contrast to only 1% of naïve animals (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, fifth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: HPL-2 does not exist in a complex with MUT-7.
claims.source: Thus, neither does HPL-2 exist in a complex with MUT-7 nor is it required to promote the association between MUT-7 and EGL-4.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results in hpl-2 mutants.

claims.claim: HPL-2 is not required to promote the association between MUT-7 and EGL-4.
claims.source: Thus, neither does HPL-2 exist in a complex with MUT-7 nor is it required to promote the association between MUT-7 and EGL-4.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the BiFC results in hpl-2 mutants.

claims.claim: 91.5% of odor-trained worms expressing HIS-71 and HPL-2 BiFC constructs showed BiFC.
claims.source: When we expressed HIS-71 tagged with the Venus N-terminus and HPL-2 tagged with the Venus C-terminus in wild-type animals, we found that 91.5% of odor-trained worms showed BiFC, in contrast to a background rate of 11.6% in naïve worms (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, sixth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: 11.6% of naïve worms expressing HIS-71 and HPL-2 BiFC constructs showed BiFC.
claims.source: When we expressed HIS-71 tagged with the Venus N-terminus and HPL-2 tagged with the Venus C-terminus in wild-type animals, we found that 91.5% of odor-trained worms showed BiFC, in contrast to a background rate of 11.6% in naïve worms (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, sixth row).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BiFC data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Odor training increases the association between HPL-2 and H3.3.
claims.source: Thus, odor training increases the association between HPL-2 and H3.3.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased BiFC signal in odor-trained animals.

claims.claim: Less than 4% of either naïve or odor-trained mut-7(pk204) mutant animals expressing HIS-71 and HPL-2 BiFC constructs exhibited the BiFC signal.
claims.source: To determine whether MUT-7 is required for the increased association, the same set of BiFC constructs was expressed in the mut-7(pk204) mutant background, and less than 4% of either naïve or odor-trained animals exhibited the BiFC signal (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, seventh row).

results.result: C. elegans MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 are orthologs of human WRN protein domains, with MUT-7 sharing 29% identity with the exonuclease domain and CeWRN-1 sharing 43% identity with the helicase domain. Loss of CeWRN-1 causes progeroid phenotypes in worms, and WS patients show brain atrophy.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 establish the evolutionary relationship between C. elegans proteins and human WRN through cited sequence identity data (C1, C2) and phenotypic parallels between worm mutants and human patients (C3, C4). All claims are supported by appropriate citations to prior work.

results.result: Prolonged odor exposure in C. elegans causes behavioral plasticity through nuclear translocation of EGL-4, which drives transcriptional silencing of odr-1 via HPL-2 loading and 22G siRNA synthesis requiring MUT-7 exonuclease activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C10 describe the established molecular pathway for olfactory learning in C. elegans, all supported by citations to prior work (Colbert and Bargmann 1997; L'Etoile et al. 2002; Lee et al. 2010a; L'Etoile and Bargmann 2000; Juang et al. 2013; Glazov et al. 2003). This provides essential background context for the current study.

results.result: MUT-7 and CeWRN-1 are both required for olfactory learning in C. elegans, and genetic epistasis analysis demonstrates they act in the same pathway in AWC neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C12, C14, and C59 are supported by behavioral chemotaxis data in Figure 1B showing that mut-7 and Cewrn-1 single mutants and double mutants all fail to learn. The similar phenotypes of single and double mutants provide standard genetic evidence for pathway placement. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05).

results.result: Different mut-7 alleles have distinct phenotypes: the E437K mutation (ne4255) disrupts chemotaxis, while the W812Amber mutation (pk204) maintains chemotaxis but abolishes learning and reduces 22G RNA levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C13, C15, and C16 are supported by behavioral data (Figure 1C) and RT-qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). The differential phenotypes of the two alleles provide insight into separable functions of MUT-7. C13 cites prior structural predictions (Gu et al. 2009).

results.result: MUT-7 is required for odor-induced downregulation of both odr-1 mRNA and ODR-1 protein through synthesis of odr-1 22G RNA. Expression of GFP-MUT-7 in AWC neurons rescues learning and 22G RNA levels in mut-7 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C24 are supported by multiple complementary datasets: behavioral rescue (Figure 2B), RT-qPCR showing 22G RNA restoration (Figure 2C), RT-qPCR showing mRNA downregulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), and fluorescence microscopy showing ODR-1::GFP protein downregulation (Figure 2D). The convergence of evidence across RNA and protein levels strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: MUT-7 has distinct functions in cytoplasm and nucleus: cytoplasmic MUT-7 is sufficient for 22G RNA synthesis but not for learning, while nuclear MUT-7 is required for learning. Both pools must act in coordination, and 22G RNA production alone is insufficient for learning.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C33 are supported by subcellular localization experiments using compartment-restricted MUT-7 constructs (Figure 2A-C). The key finding that cytoplasmic MUT-7 produces normal 22G RNA levels but fails to restore learning (C25-C26) demonstrates that 22G RNA is necessary but not sufficient. The rescue by co-expression of cytoplasmic and nuclear forms (C28) confirms both pools are required. This is a critical mechanistic insight.

results.result: The learning defects in animals expressing compartment-restricted MUT-7 or lacking CeWRN-1 are not due to developmental defects in AWC cell fate, as assessed by asymmetric STR-2 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C34, C35, and C64 are supported by STR-2 expression analysis (Supplementary file 1) showing >96% normal asymmetric expression in all tested genotypes. This control experiment rules out an important alternative explanation for the behavioral phenotypes.

results.result: MUT-7 and EGL-4 interact in the AWC nucleus of odor-trained animals, as demonstrated by BiFC. The interaction occurs in only one AWC neuron per animal, consistent with butanone being sensed by a single AWC.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C43 are supported by BiFC data (Figure 3B-C) showing 75% of odor-trained animals exhibit nuclear fluorescence versus 1% of naive animals. The single-neuron specificity (C40) matches known AWC asymmetry (C41, cited to Wes and Bargmann 2001). C36-C37 cite prior genetic epistasis data (Juang et al. 2013).

results.result: The interaction between MUT-7 and EGL-4 requires PKG phosphorylation sites in MUT-7. Mutation of all seven sites or the single S883A mutation blocks BiFC, while the control S516A mutation does not. This suggests EGL-4 binds phosphorylated MUT-7 and may phosphorylate it.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C49 are supported by BiFC data (Figure 3C) showing that phosphorylation site mutations block the interaction. However, C46-C47 are speculative—the data show phosphorylation sites are required for interaction but do not demonstrate that EGL-4 directly phosphorylates MUT-7 (no in vitro kinase assay). The authors acknowledge this limitation. The conclusion that phosphorylation is required is supported, but the identity of the kinase remains uncertain.

results.result: Cytoplasmic 22G RNA production is required for the nuclear MUT-7-EGL-4 interaction, and this requirement is mediated by NRDE-3 import of 22G RNA into the nucleus. The cytoplasmic and nuclear pools of MUT-7 do not need to shuttle between compartments.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C58 are supported by BiFC experiments showing that: (1) the W812Amber mutant that blocks 22G RNA production also blocks MUT-7-EGL-4 interaction (C50-C51); (2) co-expression of compartment-restricted forms rescues learning (C52); (3) loss of NRDE-3 blocks MUT-7-EGL-4 interaction even with constitutively nuclear proteins (C55-C57). This demonstrates that nuclear import of 22G RNA by NRDE-3 is required for the nuclear interaction. The logic is sound and the controls are appropriate.

results.result: CeWRN-1 acts within AWC neurons to promote olfactory plasticity, localizes to the AWC nucleus, and does not regulate EGL-4 nuclear entry.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C63, C65-C66 are supported by: expression pattern analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), cell-specific rescue (Figure 4B), nuclear localization (Figure 4B), and EGL-4 localization in Cewrn-1 mutants (Supplementary file 2). The data clearly establish that CeWRN-1 functions in AWC neurons and acts downstream of or parallel to EGL-4 nuclear entry.

results.result: CeWRN-1 and MUT-7 interact in the nucleus of odor-trained animals (46% BiFC signal) in an NRDE-3-dependent manner. CeWRN-1 does not interact directly with EGL-4 (<2% BiFC signal).
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C72 are supported by BiFC data (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4C-D). The strong odor-dependent CeWRN-1-MUT-7 interaction (46% vs <4% in controls) and its dependence on NRDE-3 (only 3% in nrde-3 mutants) are clearly demonstrated. The lack of CeWRN-1-EGL-4 interaction provides important negative control data.

results.result: MUT-7 and HPL-2 do not directly associate, and HPL-2 is not required for the MUT-7-EGL-4 interaction, as shown by BiFC experiments in wild-type and hpl-2 mutant backgrounds.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C77 are supported by BiFC data (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) showing very low BiFC signal between MUT-7 and HPL-2 (<4%) and normal MUT-7-EGL-4 interaction in hpl-2 mutants (67%). This rules out a model where MUT-7, EGL-4, and HPL-2 exist in a single complex.

results.result: Odor training increases the association between HPL-2 and histone H3.3 (from 11.6% to 91.5% BiFC signal), and this increased association requires MUT-7 but not direct MUT-7-HPL-2 interaction. This suggests phosphorylated MUT-7 directs heterochromatin complex formation, possibly using 22G RNA as a guide.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C83 are supported by BiFC data (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) showing dramatic odor-induced increase in HPL-2-H3.3 interaction and its dependence on MUT-7. C84 is speculative but reasonable given the data. The model that MUT-7 directs HPL-2 to specific loci via 22G RNA guidance is consistent with all observations, though direct evidence for the guidance mechanism is not provided.

results.result: CeWRN-1 and HPL-2 act in the same genetic pathway and interact in odor-trained animals (80% BiFC signal) in an NRDE-3-dependent manner. CeWRN-1 is required for HPL-2 to associate with histone H3 in odor-trained animals.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C92 are supported by genetic epistasis (Figure 1B), BiFC data showing CeWRN-1-HPL-2 interaction (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), NRDE-3 dependence (Figure 4D), and reduced HPL-2-H3 interaction in Cewrn-1 mutants (Figure 4A). This establishes CeWRN-1 as a critical link between the siRNA pathway and heterochromatin formation.

results.result: CeWRN-1 is not required for basal or odor-induced odr-1 22G RNA synthesis, indicating that endogenous MUT-7 functions normally in Cewrn-1 mutants. CeWRN-1 acts downstream of 22G RNA synthesis to promote HPL-2 loading onto histone H3.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C98 are supported by RT-qPCR data (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) showing normal 22G RNA levels in Cewrn-1 mutants but reduced levels in mut-7 mutants. This clearly separates the functions of MUT-7 (22G RNA synthesis) and CeWRN-1 (downstream chromatin remodeling) and establishes their epistatic relationship.

results.result: Loss of CeWRN-1 modestly reduces brood size (213 to 185 eggs), while loss of MUT-7 severely reduces brood size (96 eggs) and increases germ cell corpses. The MUT-7 exonuclease is required for germ cell viability, but the CeWRN-1 helicase may not be sufficient.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C105 are supported by brood size data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and cell corpse counts (Figure 5—figure supplements 2-3). The data clearly show differential effects of the two proteins on fertility. However, C105 is somewhat speculative—the data show CeWRN-1 has a milder effect than MUT-7, but whether it is 'not sufficient' is not definitively established. The conclusion about MUT-7 requirement (C104) is well-supported.

results.result: The exonuclease and helicase domains of WRN are conserved and functionally important across species. In C. elegans, MUT-7 is involved in germline transposon silencing via 22G RNA production, and loss of MUT-7 leads to transposon activation and DNA damage.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C111 are all supported by citations to prior work (Ketting et al. 1999; Suzuki et al. 1999; Perry et al. 2006; Gu et al. 2009; Halic and Moazed 2009; Wallis et al. 2019). This provides important context for understanding the evolutionary conservation and broader biological roles of the proteins studied.

results.result: The current work demonstrates that prolonged odor stimulation activates 22G RNA synthesis via cytoplasmic MUT-7, and nuclear import of siRNA by NRDE-3 promotes HPL-2 loading onto specific loci to repress ODR-1 expression and direct olfactory plasticity. MUT-7 acts in both cytoplasm (siRNA synthesis) and nucleus (association with CeWRN-1).
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113, C115, C117-C120 summarize the major findings of the current study, all of which are supported by the experimental data described in previous result groups. This represents the core mechanistic model emerging from the work.

results.result: The findings suggest that the exonuclease and helicase domains of human WRN may act in concert to promote RNA-dependent loading into a heterochromatin complex, and failure of this process may reduce plasticity in postmitotic neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C121-C122 are speculative extrapolations from the C. elegans data to human WRN function. While the evolutionary conservation and phenotypic parallels provide some support, direct evidence for this mechanism in mammalian neurons is lacking. The authors appropriately use cautious language ('may act', 'suggest'). This represents a reasonable hypothesis for future testing but is not directly demonstrated.

results.result: Clinical and genetic evidence from human WS patients and model organisms suggests that WRN exonuclease activity may be more critical than helicase activity for preventing disease, and that WRN may play important roles in neuronal development and neuroplasticity.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C132 are all supported by citations to prior clinical and genetic studies (Yu et al. 1996; Huang et al. 2006; Kamath-Loeb et al. 2017; Oshima and Hisama 2014; Lessel et al. 2015; Fang et al. 2019). C132 is somewhat speculative but based on cited microarray data. This provides important clinical context for the mechanistic findings.

results.result: Small RNAs show differential expression in WS mouse models, and recent reports suggest human WS may result from changes in epigenetic marks such as DNA methylation patterns rather than loss of genome integrity.
results.evaluation: Claims C114 and C116 are supported by citations to prior work (Dallaire et al. 2012; Maierhofer et al. 2019). This provides important context suggesting that the siRNA-mediated epigenetic mechanism discovered in C. elegans may be relevant to human disease.

results.result: The observation that CeWRN-1 associates with HPL-2 and promotes HPL-2-H3 interaction is consistent with prior findings that human WRN associates with HP1 and H3K9me3 in human WS mesenchymal stem cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C93 is supported by citation to Zhang et al. 2015. This parallel between worm and human provides important validation that the mechanism discovered in C. elegans may be conserved in mammals.
